questions.question_text: Choose the correct comparison between $\frac{1}{7}$ and $\frac{1}{2}$.

options.why: This treats a larger denominator as a larger unit fraction.
This ignores that fifths and halves are different-sized parts.

questions.question_text: Which unit fraction equals one half?

options.why: Thirds are smaller than halves because there are more equal parts.
This is not a unit fraction and equals two wholes.

questions.solution_text:
A unit fraction equal to a half has denominator $2$.
$\frac{1}{2}$

options.text: Eight equal parts are smaller than two equal parts.
Eight is greater than two, so the fraction is greater.
options.why: This transfers whole-number order directly to unit fractions.
No addition is involved in comparing these fractions.

questions.solution_text:
The same whole is split into more pieces.
Each eighth is smaller than each half.

questions.question_text: A proper unit fraction has denominator $n>2$. How does it compare with $\frac{1}{2}$?

options.why: This reverses the unit-fraction denominator rule.
Only a denominator of two gives exactly one half.

questions.solution_text:
$n>2$ means the whole is split into more than two equal parts.
$\frac{1}{n}<\frac{1}{2}$

questions.question_text: Which unit fraction is closest to $\frac{1}{2}$ without equalling it?

options.why: A fourth is farther below one half than a third.
A tenth is much farther below one half.
One whole is not a proper unit fraction below one half.

questions.solution_text:
Among denominators greater than $2$, the smallest is $3$.
$\frac{1}{3}$ is closest below $\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.question_text: Which statement about proper unit fractions is true?

options.text: $\frac{1}{2}$ is the greatest proper unit fraction.

options.why: This treats the larger denominator as the larger value.

options.text: All unit fractions equal one another.
options.why: Equal numerators do not make fractions with different denominators equal.

questions.solution_text:
As the denominator increases, a unit fraction decreases.
$\frac{1}{2}$ is therefore the greatest proper unit fraction.
